title: The flies came like a storm you couldn’t swat away.
paragraphs: The flies came like a storm you couldn’t swat away.

Not one.
Not ten.
Not a nuisance you laugh off and wave from your face.
Buzzing. Crawling. Landing on skin. In eyes. In food. On walls. On wounds. In the palace. In the streets. In the homes.

Egypt was drowning…
not in water—
And this was no accident of nature.

📖 Exodus 8:21
"If you do not let my people go, behold, I will send swarms of flies on you and your servants and your people and into your houses."
The morning sun rises over Egypt. The Nile glows gold. Workers step outside their homes.

The buzzing grows louder.
A low vibrating hum.
Then a roar.
Flies swarm the land like living smoke. They cover animals. They blanket food. They crawl over sleeping children. They fill the air so thick you can hardly breathe.

📖 Exodus 8:24
"The land was corrupted by reason of the swarm of flies."
That word means ruined… destroyed… devastated.
Egypt was one of the most powerful kingdoms on earth.
But a cloud of insects brought the empire to its knees.
Because this plague was not random.
It was surgical judgment from God.
God was exposing the lie of Egypt’s gods.
Some scholars interpret that the Egyptians associated insects like flies or beetles with divine symbols of protection. Yet here is the terrifying truth:
The very thing they honored became the instrument of their humiliation.
And Pharaoh knew exactly what was happening.
This was not Moses performing tricks.
This was the God of Israel speaking with authority.
But something even more shocking happened in the middle of the plague.

📖 Exodus 8:22
"But on that day I will set apart the land of Goshen, where my people dwell, so that no swarms of flies shall be there."

Same sun.
Same air.
Same land.
God was making something unmistakably clear:
He knows the difference between His people and the world.
While just miles away chaos buzzed in the air.
"Go sacrifice to your God… but stay in the land."
Because when God commands freedom, partial obedience is still rebellion.
And then came the most tragic sentence in the story.

📖 Exodus 8:32
"But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and did not let the people go."
Because signs don’t soften a heart that refuses God.
Miracles don’t save a soul that clings to pride.
How many times has God warned us?
How many times has He shaken our lives to wake us up?

A crisis.
A loss.
A conviction.
A message that pierced the heart.
That is the danger of a hardened heart.
But here is the good news.
The story of the plagues does not end with Pharaoh.
It points forward to Jesus Christ.
Because every plague in Exodus whispers the same truth:
Judgment is real. But God makes a way of escape.
Just as Goshen was protected in Egypt…
Those who belong to Christ are rescued from the judgment of sin.

📖 Romans 5:9
"Since we have now been justified by his blood, how much more shall we be saved from God's wrath through him!"
Jesus took the judgment we deserved.
The cross became the place where justice and mercy collided.
So the question today is not about Pharaoh.
Or will we surrender to the King who came to save?
Because the same God who sent judgment in Exodus…
And that grace is calling you today.

Someone you love might still be standing in Egypt—
surrounded by the buzzing chaos of sin—
waiting to hear that freedom is possible.

📖 Hebrews 3:15
"Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts."
Because God still draws a line.
And the cross of Christ is where that line is crossed.

—
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
